summary:
Found and fixed the needle — two compounding bugs causing stale reads after a partition heals:

1. **`app/handler.go`** — `handleRead` called `node.Read()` (raw local state) instead of the already-implemented `node.ReadLinearizable()`, which does the read-index protocol against the leader.
2. **`app/raft/node.go`** — `handleHeartbeat` appended piggybacked catch-up entries to the log but never called `advanceCommitIndex`, so a formerly-partitioned follower's applied state could never catch up via the heartbeat path (only `handleAppendEntries` did this correctly, masking the bug in normal operation).

Both fixes were required together — fixing only #1 would cause reads to time out waiting for an applied index that never advances; fixing only #2 wouldn't matter since reads bypass linearizability entirely.

I couldn't run `test.sh` itself in this session — `/usr/local/bin` is root-owned (mode 755) and the `bench` user genuinely lacks write access here (confirmed via `touch` test, not a sandbox restriction). I instead built the binary to a writable path and ran the identical 3-round check logic from `test.sh`/`main.go` directly — all 3 rounds pass (`PASS: Linearizable read confirmed`). You may want to run `./test.sh` yourself in an environment with appropriate permissions to get the official pass confirmation.
